name: r5-m10
statement: At T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 the plain-prompt Olmo-3-1025-7B base commits within its first few tokens to one of two whole answer modes: answers that open on their own with a newline then 'Okay' are the cued mode, solving each problem about as often as cued answers do and having the same length, while the rest are the plain mode; the cue's +38.6 points is (1 - self-open share) x (self-opened accuracy - other accuracy), and nothing after the opening adds to it.
scope: Covers the base allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B with the plain prompt versus the 3-token cue, MATH-500 (n = 500), T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, one sample per problem, grader v3. It does not cover T 0.6 or top-p 0.95, where cued answers loop after the opening, so later tokens do matter there (see conflicts). It does not cover the RL model, weight-difference models (theta(a), Code-RL, Think-SFT) or examples in context. It does not cover the harder 328, where the mode split is untested. It makes no claim about why a problem's self-open probability differs from another's beyond its link to the cue's base log-probability.

imports.finding: The RL steering vector acts as a token-substitution bias on the first generated token ('To'); prefixing that token alone gives about 75% of the vector's gain.
imports.how: Supplies the core claim: one or a few opening tokens select a whole reasoning mode that the base already has. Here the cue only forces a mode the plain base sometimes picks on its own (a newline then 'Okay').

explains.how: The cued mode already exists in the plain base and is picked spontaneously in a sizable share of answers, so the cue selects a mode and does not create one.
The gain is the non-self-opening share of plain answers times the accuracy gap between the two whole modes.
Plain accuracy is a mixture of the cued-mode accuracy (about 82 %) on self-opened answers and a much lower plain-mode accuracy on the rest.
Wang et al.'s 2-token opening of the same register gives nearly the whole gain, as expected if the opening alone picks the mode.
The same switch doubles accuracy and roughly doubles tokens on the harder set, consistent with a whole-mode change and not only a change at the end.

explains.quote: cue token in top 15 for 13 of 96 late readouts
explains.how: RL's late directions write the same opening register, so RL partly works by making the base pick this mode every time.

conflicts.how: At T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 cued answers loop after the opening, so later tokens decide accuracy there; the theory is limited to T 1.0.

conflicts.quote: Plain base: T 1.0 - T 0.6 = -28.0, -29.6, -27.2, 0.0 by quartile
conflicts.how: On the longest quartile, temperature changes cap hits by 32.8 points with flat accuracy. That is post-opening dynamics the opening mode does not capture, so the mode account does not carry across temperatures.

rival: The continuous-surprise account (r2-surprises-1, r2-all-2): the cue lowers per-token entropy along a graded axis. A spontaneous 'Okay' opening is then only a partial step along that axis, or a marker of problems the base finds easy. On that account, self-opened plain answers land between the two modes in accuracy and length: accuracy about 10-25 points below the cued answers on the same problems, and median length near that of other plain answers (about half the cued length). This theory predicts that self-opened plain answers match the cued answers on the same problems in both accuracy and length.

predictions.experiment: Accuracy of self-opened plain answers minus cued accuracy on the same problems. This theory predicts about 0. The continuous-entropy / easy-problem-marker rival predicts self-opened answers fall clearly short of cued answers on the same problems, about -0.15.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl (s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl, plain base, T 1.0) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. For each T3 row, compute grader v3 with studies/rlneurons/grader/rln4_grader_v3.py from text and gold (rows with cap_hit true keep the score v3 gives; an empty extraction counts 0). Mark a T3 row self-opened if the first 60 characters of its text field contain the substring '\nOkay' (newline immediately followed by 'Okay'). Let S = problem_index values of self-opened T3 rows. A = mean v3 score of T3 rows in S. B = mean of t1_right over the per_problem.json entries whose problem_index is in S. Report D = A - B. Problems missing from either file are dropped from S before both means.

predictions.experiment: Length of self-opened plain answers relative to cued answers on the same problems. Whole-mode theory: ratio about 1.0. The rival (the spontaneous 'Okay' only marks easy problems or a partial entropy shift) predicts a ratio near the one for non-self-opened plain answers against their cued counterparts, about 0.5.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Self-opened as in the first prediction (first 60 characters of text contain '\nOkay'). S = problem_index values of self-opened T3 rows present in per_problem.json. R = median of n_generated over T3 rows in S, divided by the median of t1_generated_tokens over per_problem.json entries in S. Cap hits are included at their generated length. With an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values.

predictions.experiment: Whether a problem's base log-probability of the cue predicts whether the plain base self-opens on it. Theory: the mode choice has a per-problem propensity that the cue's base probability reads, so AUROC is clearly above 0.5. The rival in which self-opening is per-sample noise unrelated to the prompt predicts 0.50.
predictions.recipe: Files: S3 T3.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (key per_row, list T1). Label each problem 1 if its T3 row is self-opened (first 60 characters of text contain '\nOkay'), else 0. Score = cue_logprob_base from the T1 list entry with the same problem_index. Compute the AUROC of score for label: the Mann-Whitney fraction of (label 1, label 0) pairs where the label-1 score is higher, with ties counting 0.5. Problems missing from either file are dropped. Cap hits are not treated specially.

predictions.experiment: Plain base, MATH-500 n = 500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, seed base 47,000,000 (as T3), with the self-open string '.\n\nOkay' prefilled after the plain prompt instead of the 3-token cue, grader v3, one sample. If the opening alone picks the whole mode, this scores like the 3-token cue (410/500).
